title: Tirisfal Glades
body: Tirisfal Glades was once the heartland of the kingdom of Lordaeron, a country of misty woods, quiet farms and noble estates in the shadow of the royal capital. When the Plague of Undeath swept through, so many died that mass graves had to be dug, and much of the population rose again as servants of the Scourge. Now the glades belong to the Forsaken, the undead who broke free of the Lich King under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. From the Undercity beneath the ruined capital and from the town of Brill, the Deathguard fight on several fronts at once. Mindless dead still shamble through Deathknell and hold the Agamand Mills, Rot Hide gnolls rob the graves for the Lich King, and more undead slip in past the Bulwark from the Plaguelands. In the northeast the Scarlet Crusade holds its great monastery and sends zealots across the glades to purge every undead they find, free-willed or not.

title: Deathknell
body: In the hills of western Tirisfal lies Deathknell, where many of the Forsaken first open their eyes to their new existence. The newly risen wake in the crypt above the village, the Shadow Grave, tended by its caretaker Undertaker Mordo, who is ready to toss onto the fire any who fail to stir. Down the road in the chapel, Shadow Priest Sarvis explains to each confused arrival that the Dark Lady has freed them from the Lich King. Executor Arren commands the village, Deathguard Saltain sends recruits to scavenge for usable gear, and Novice Elreth tends the wounded. Mindless zombies and ghouls, their former kin, still wander the northern streets, and a Scarlet Crusade detachment has camped to the southeast.

title: Night Web's Hollow
body: Northwest of Deathknell lies Night Web's Hollow, a small valley around the mouth of an old gold mine. Gold was scarce even when the Alliance stood at the height of its power, and the Forsaken badly need the ore, but spiders have overrun the valley and the tunnels alike. Young spiders prowl the open ground while larger night webs lurk in the shadowed depths of the mine. Executor Arren can spare few hands for the work, so the hollow is being cleared bit by bit. He expects weeks or months to pass before the infestation is gone and the webbing can finally be burned away with torches.

title: Solliden Farmstead
body: North of Deathknell, the Solliden Farmstead is a rare sight in Tirisfal: a farm still worked by living humans. Farmer Solliden and his hands tend their pumpkin fields with the Scarlet Crusade close by, its warriors holding a tower to the west beyond the farm, and the farmers side with the Crusaders against all undead. To the Forsaken they are a blight on the land. Deathguard Simmer keeps watch on the road nearby and sends young recruits to steal the farm's pumpkins, which the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill has found a sinister use for.

title: Cold Hearth Manor
body: Cold Hearth Manor stands beside the main road southwest of Brill, just across a bridge. It was once a farm known for its welcoming hearth and bountiful crops, but the Plague killed everyone who lived and worked there, and its fields have long since gone barren. The Forsaken have taken over the farmhouse, where the tailors Bowen and Constance Brisboise ply their trade for passing travelers. The country around it is far from safe. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses have trickled into the lands west of Brill near the old bridge, and the Deathguard reward those who beat them back.

title: Brill
body: Brill was a human town of the Lordaeron countryside and one of the first to fall to the Plague of Undeath. Today it is the main Forsaken town of the glades, just north of the ruined capital. Magistrate Sevren governs from the town hall, while Executor Zygand directs the Deathguard against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. Apothecaries pursue their experiments, a wanted poster calls for the death of the gnoll Maggot Eye, and the Gallows' End Tavern serves as inn and prison both. North of the town, near the graveyard, stands a sealed mausoleum where the Deathguard hold Ulag the Cleaver, a captured Scourge agent still in thrall to the Lich King.

title: Gallows' End Tavern
body: The Gallows' End Tavern stands on the southeast edge of Brill. Innkeeper Renee offers the weary dead a place to rest their bones, a mage trainer who checked in too late to get a room teaches from the upstairs landing, and Coleman Farthing nurses his bitter grudge against the Agamand family. The cellar has a grimmer purpose. The Deathguard keep prisoners there until they can be properly dealt with, among them a Scarlet zealot and a dwarven mountaineer, and the apothecaries of Brill find such captives convenient subjects for testing their latest brews.

title: Agamand Mills
body: Northwest of Brill, a cluster of windmills marks the Agamand Mills, once the seat of the most prosperous family in Tirisfal. When the Scourge came, the Agamands fortified their home and persuaded their workers to stay and defend it. The defense failed, and the family and their people perished. Now the Scourge mean to make the mills a base for further attacks on the Forsaken. Skeletal soldiers and darkeye bonecasters crowd the fields, lost souls drift among the windmills, and the dead Agamands themselves walk the grounds as minions of the Lich King.

title: Agamand Family Crypt
body: At the north end of the Agamand Mills stands the family crypt, where generations of Agamands were laid to rest. It is now the strongest Scourge position in the area and the headquarters of Captain Dargol, a skeletal commander who uses necromancy to raise the Agamand ancestors from their tombs. Wailing and rotting dead fill the grounds, ready to be turned against the Forsaken. The crypt also guards the family's heirloom weapons, a sword, an axe, a dagger and a mace, which Coleman Farthing would dearly like to see stripped from the cursed Agamand lands.

title: Garren's Haunt
body: North of Brill, Garren's Haunt was once a prosperous farmstead of farmhouse, barn and wide fields. The Scourge murdered Garren and his family when Lordaeron fell, and the gray, lifeless farm is now the den of the Rot Hide gnolls, corpse thieves in the service of the Scourge who attack anyone who strays too close. The foulest of them is Maggot Eye. To the southwest lie the mass graves dug for the countless dead of the Plague, and the gnolls dig there for bodies to carry off and swell the Lich King's armies.

title: Gunther's Retreat
body: On an island in Brightwater Lake, northeast of Brill, a lone lich has made his home at Gunther's Retreat. He is free of the Lich King's will, yet believes every other undead is still a Scourge slave, and he sets his minions on anyone who approaches, Forsaken included. Hungering dead and shambling horrors guard the island. Off its southern shore stands an old, bloody table used as an altar by Lillith Nefara, a powerful agent of the Scourge, who wakes in wrath when a Candle of Beckoning is lit upon it.

title: Balnir Farmstead
body: The Balnir Farmstead lies in eastern Tirisfal on the way to the Plaguelands. Its family once bred the white horses ridden by Lordaeron's royal household. Today the ruined farm is a haven for Scourge that slip past the Bulwark, bleeding horrors and wandering spirits among them, and the Deathguard patrol it closely. Mages of the Undercity gather the snapdragons in its garden, a flower highly receptive to magic, to learn whether the taint of the Plaguelands has crept into Tirisfal.

title: Crusader Outpost
body: Crusader Outpost is a ruined tower in eastern Tirisfal near the Balnir Farmstead, held by the Scarlet Crusade to watch the main road through the glades. Its garrison of Scarlet friars answers to Captain Vachon and raids out from the tower against the undead. Executor Zygand of Brill reckons that cutting down the captain and his friars would be a devastating blow to the Crusade in the glades.

title: Venomweb Vale
body: Venomweb Vale is a wide valley in eastern Tirisfal, just south of the Scarlet Monastery. It was once a fine hunting ground for deer and rabbits, but it now crawls with vicious night web spiders and takes its new name from them. Their venom is prized by the apothecaries of Brill, who believe it preserves the deadly agent of an ancient plague. The spiders gather around a monstrous one called Sri'skulk. Old tales say the vale was once a meeting place of the Council of Tirisfal, and that one of its members bred the spiders to guard it.

title: Whispering Gardens
body: The Whispering Gardens spread across the hill below the entrance of the Scarlet Monastery, the great seat of the Scarlet Crusade in northeastern Tirisfal. Long ago a fierce battle was fought here between a Scourge host and the forces that would become the Crusade, and it is said the spirits of the fallen still murmur in the twilight. Today the gardens, and the hedged Terrace of Repose on the far side of the monastery doors, are thick with Scarlet scouts, magicians and preservers, who guard the approach to the monastery against undead and outsiders alike.

title: Scarlet Watch Post
body: North of the Scarlet Monastery, the Scarlet Watch Post is a scout tower guarding the monastery's less defensible northern side. It stands past Faol's Rest, where the revered Archbishop Alonsus Faol was laid to rest some time before the Plague. The tower's crew of neophytes and vanguards is led by Captain Melrache, a ruthless commander who keeps two bodyguards at his side and raids across northern Tirisfal.

title: Ruins of Lordaeron
body: South of Brill rise the Ruins of Lordaeron, all that remains of the capital where King Terenas Menethil ruled. In its throne room the king was slain by his own son, Prince Arthas, and the Scourge laid the city waste. A grave in the ruins honors Terenas as the last true king of Lordaeron, praying that the father lie blameless for the deeds of the son. Beneath lies the Undercity, capital of the Forsaken, reached by lifts at the back of the ruins, and zeppelins from outside the walls link it with distant lands.

Varimathras and Putress had betrayed the Dark Lady and seized the city below, and the Horde massed among these broken walls to take it back. Warsong battleguards and siege engines filled the ruins, Vol'jin held the ground for the Warchief, and Thrall and Lady Sylvanas came here to give the order to attack.

title: The Bulwark
body: The Bulwark guards the eastern edge of Tirisfal where the road enters the Western Plaguelands, the Forsaken's last line of defense against the Scourge beyond. High Executor Derrington commands this front, where politics give way to a daily fight for survival and the defenders press toward Andorhal. Members of the Argent Dawn, an order that calls both Horde and Alliance its friends in the war on evil, stand alongside the Forsaken, and apothecaries prepare agents to turn the Scourge's plague cauldrons against their makers. Even so, some undead still slip past into the glades.

title: Executor Zygand
body: Executor Zygand commands the Deathguard in Brill, with officers such as Executor Arren at Deathknell and Deathguard Linnea at the eastern waystation reporting to him. With the Lich King's army growing each night the Deathguard have larger worries, so Zygand looks to recruits with initiative to drive the Scarlet Crusade to the grave. He has little patience for those who idle in Brill while their people need them in the field, and he prizes ruthlessness in those who serve the Dark Lady under him.

When Captain Melrache, the last of the Crusade captains he sent the Deathguard after, falls, Zygand is well pleased. Ruthless fighters who conquer in the name of the Forsaken, he says, bring his people one step closer to defeating Arthas once and for all, and he has a good feeling about the comrade who did the work.

title: Magistrate Sevren
body: Magistrate Sevren governs Brill from its town hall, a brisk official who keeps the town's records of the dead and directs its struggle against the Scourge. He relies on fresh reports from the Deathguard waystation near the Plaguelands border, sends agents to stop the Rot Hide gnolls robbing the mass graves, and has marked the Scourge stronghold in the Agamand Family Crypt for destruction. When Bethor Iceshard of the Undercity asked for an agent of proven worth against the Scourge for a dangerous errand, it was Sevren who chose one and sent them south with his orders.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Magistrate_Sevren (Brill Town Hall, known for being brisk)

title: Shadow Priest Sarvis
body: Shadow Priest Sarvis waits in the chapel at the foot of the hill in Deathknell, and for many newly risen Forsaken he is the first to explain what has become of them. He tells each one that Lady Sylvanas has freed them from the Lich King, and that the Forsaken now wage war on the Scourge and on the holdouts of humanity alike. No other race on Azeroth, he says, has suffered as their people have, and laughing in the face of death is now second nature to them. He sends every recruit against the mindless dead of the village, regretting only that such numbers cannot be brought into the fold.
notes: Check: ok. Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Gunther Arcanus
body: Gunther Arcanus is the lich of Brightwater Lake, who keeps to his island at Gunther's Retreat northeast of Brill. He fell to the Plague but has broken free of the Lich King's hold, and he has grown powerful in death. Yet he believes every other undead is still a Scourge slave, and he sets his minions on all who come near, Forsaken included. To the Forsaken a free-willed lich is well worth winning over, for his knowledge of necromancy could serve the Dark Lady well.
sources: quest 366 description (Kirin Tor students; both fell to the Plague)
quest 357 description and reward text (skilled necromancer in life)
notes: Check: ok. Converted: his past (Kirin Tor, Bethor, Thule) moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 357, where Bethor recognises the book, and QUEST_ACCEPT 366, the entry trigger where he tells it); the returned book and his demand moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 366); Lillith's death and the Nether Gem moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 409). The opening keeps only what quest 357 says of him. Earlier: 'By his own will' softened; quest 357/409 support only that he is free-willed and thought himself alone.

parts.body: His spellbook gives away who he was. In life Gunther was a skilled necromancer who studied among the Kirin Tor of Dalaran with his friends Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw. Gunther and Bethor both fell to the Plague, while Thule went over to the Scourge. Bethor, free himself and serving the Dark Lady, rejoices to learn that his old friend is free too.

The book comes back to Gunther bearing a new enchantment, and he knows it for Bethor's work. If Bethor still exists, he wonders, perhaps he too escaped the Lich King. Still he trusts no stranger, and demands proof: Lillith Nefara, a Scourge agent who wakes at a bloody altar off his island, must be destroyed.

Lillith Nefara falls, and Gunther is astonished. He had believed himself the only undead with free will, but now he knows others have broken the Lich King's domination. He sends a Nether Gem to his old comrade Bethor, so that the two can speak again, for he has much to tell him.

title: Coleman and Yvette Farthing
body: Coleman Farthing worked the Agamand Mills before the Plague. When the Scourge came, the Agamands fortified their home and talked their workers into staying to defend it, and Coleman, a loyal fool by his own account, was doomed to undeath by their pride. Now a Forsaken at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, he blames the family for all he lost, and since the dead Agamands walk the mills as servants of the Scourge, he wants their remains destroyed and brought to him. His daughter Yvette has risen among the Forsaken too and keeps near him in Brill. Thurman, the eldest Agamand son, was once her beloved.
sources: quest 362 reward text (bones on my mantle)

parts.body: When the remains of Gregor, Nissa and Thurman are brought to him, Coleman finds that revenge has a sweet taste. He wonders whether any free will lingered in the Agamands when they were destroyed, and hopes they knew fear before they were smashed into oblivion, though he admits it is a foolish hope.
sources: quest 354 required items 2828, 2829, 2830 (remains of Nissa, Gregor, Thurman)

parts.body: When Devlin's bones are brought to him, Coleman gives them a place on his mantle. If his cold heart can find any warmth, he says, it is in knowing the Agamands are destroyed, for they failed him and his family when the Plague came, and he swears to grind what is left of them under his heel.

Thurman's last letter reaches Yvette at last. For a moment she grieves: she begged him to leave the mills with her and her father, but his loyalty to his family was too strong. Then her face grows cold. Regrets are for the weak, she says, and as a Forsaken she has new goals, with no room for love. That life is over.

title: Devlin Agamand
body: Devlin was the younger of the two Agamand sons, weak and sharp-tongued where his brother Thurman was tall and gentle. When the Agamand Mills fell to the Plague, Coleman Farthing was not surprised to hear that Devlin was quick to succumb. He now haunts the road to the mills as a servant of the Lich King, and falls on anyone who comes to visit the family. His mad chatter carries on the wind: his family hated him and thought him weak, he is head of the family at last, and he asks his cold lord when the promise will be kept.
sources: quest 362 description (quick to succumb; mad chattering near the road)
notes: Check: ok. Converted: the betrayal (pact, murdered watchmen, the breach) moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 361, which hands over Thurman's readable letter (item 2837). The opening keeps quest 362's description and his creature_text. Earlier: Faction changed 2 to 0: Devlin (faction 21) is hostile to all and killable by Alliance; matches the original note.

parts.body: Thurman's undelivered letter tells the truth behind that chatter. Devlin, a mystery to his family since childhood, had warned them that facing the Scourge meant doom. Then he despaired and made a pact with the enemy, murdering two watchmen and letting the undead through a breach, and a third of the defenders were slain. Whatever price he was promised, Thurman was sure it was laced with lies.

title: Apothecary Johaan
body: Apothecary Johaan of the Royal Apothecary Society works in Brill on a challenge set by Lady Sylvanas herself: to brew a new plague deadlier than any ailment on Azeroth, one that will bring Arthas's Scourge to ruin. He proceeds by trial and error, testing darkhound blood, murloc scales and the venom of night web spiders, and lacing ordinary pumpkins with his formulas. His test subjects come from among the prisoners in the cellar of the Gallows' End Tavern. Mindful of his duty to the Society, he shares his findings with his colleagues at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest.
notes: Check: ok. Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Faction changed 0 to 2: Johaan uses template 68 (hostile to Alliance) and quest 367 is Horde only.

title: Maggot Eye
body: Maggot Eye is a gnoll of the Rot Hide pack, foul even by gnoll standards, who pillages the lands around Garren's Haunt north of Brill. He has been stealing corpses for the Lich King's armies, and the town of Brill has sentenced him to death for his crimes against the Forsaken. A wanted poster in town promises a reward to whoever carries out the sentence and brings his paw to Executor Zygand, and closes with a blunt reminder that mercy is for the weak.
notes: Check: ok. Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: High Executor Derrington
body: High Executor Derrington commands the Forsaken at the Bulwark on Tirisfal's eastern border. He has no patience for the schemes of politicians, for at the Bulwark survival is fought for every day, and he welcomes anyone eager to prove themselves a hero. His eyes are fixed on Andorhal and the lich Araj the Summoner who holds it. He plans to set the Scarlet Crusade and the Scourge at each other's throats with a burned command tent and a planted Scourge banner, and his second, Shadow Priestess Vandis, oversees a scheme to turn the Scourge's own plague cauldrons against them.
sources: quest 5228 description (My second, Shadow Priestess Vandis)
notes: Check: ok. Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. verified

title: Rude Awakening
body: Each new Forsaken in Deathknell begins in the cold of the crypt, greeted by Undertaker Mordo and sent down to Shadow Priest Sarvis, who explains that the Lich King's hold is broken and that the Dark Lady leads the war against the Scourge. The first lesson is to destroy the mindless zombies, ghouls and rattling skeletons in the north of the village, former brothers and sisters who remain the Lich King's slaves. Recruits scavenge the village for gear, and hunt wolves and bats so Novice Elreth can find them armor. Among these first tasks is a gentler one. Marla Fipps was spared undeath only to die at the hands of her husband Samuel, who rose as one of the mindless. Her last wish was to be buried beside him, and Samuel still roams a ruined camp northeast of the village.
notes: Check: ok. Converted: Samuel's burial moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 6395; the opening now ends on Marla's wish and where Samuel roams. Earlier: verified

parts.body: Samuel Fipps is laid to rest at last, his remains buried in Marla's grave in the first row of the village graveyard. Novice Elreth hopes the two will find peace together. The dead must be respected, she says, for that is one of the ways the Forsaken differ from the Scourge.

title: At War with the Scarlet Crusade
body: The Scarlet Crusade hunts every undead in Tirisfal, Scourge or Forsaken, and the Deathguard answer in kind. It begins at Deathknell, where Executor Arren strikes at a Crusade camp to the southeast. Word from Brill says a messenger from the Scarlet Monastery has been sent there with important information, and Arren means to have it. In Brill, Executor Zygand wants recruits with initiative to drive the zealots to the grave, starting with the Scarlet warriors at the tower beyond the Solliden Farmstead. Deathguard Burgess gathers Scarlet insignia rings as proof of loyalty to the Dark Lady and to the dreadlord Varimathras, who, Burgess says, is seeing personally to the destruction of the human race.
sources: page_text 223, 224 (Tirisfal Regional Command, by order of the Highlord)
notes: Check: part 1 now triggers on DONE 382 only and stops at what 382 and the looted documents reveal (ACCEPT 427 needs no earlier quest and reveals neither Meven nor the captains; Zygand's plan is 383's reward); part 2 picks up the documents reaching Zygand (427, 370 texts); parts 3 and 4 no longer assume the reader knows of three captains. The Varimathras line is now Burgess's claim, so it is not stated as fact at state 18 after the Battle for the Undercity. Converted: Meven Korgal's death and the documents moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 382, and QUEST_ACCEPT 427, whose text already speaks of the documents); each captain's death moved to its own part on the turn-in of 370, 371 and 372. Varimathras is now named only as the dreadlord Burgess serves, as quest 374 presents him, instead of 'then lieutenant', which hinted at his later betrayal. Earlier: Varimathras qualified as 'then' lieutenant, since by 3.3.5 he has turned traitor (Battle for the Undercity).

parts.body: The messenger, Meven Korgal, is slain at the Crusader camp. Among his scouting reports and orders lies the prize: a map of the dispositions of the Crusade's field commanders. The orders show a Tirisfal Regional Command answering to the Highlord through three captains, Perrine, Vachon and Melrache.
sources: page_text 223, 224 (item 2885 Scarlet Crusade Documents, looted from Meven Korgal 1667 and required by 382)

parts.body: Arren's papers reach Executor Zygand, and with the Crusade's positions known he strikes at its leaders. First falls Captain Perrine, cut down with zealots and missionaries of the brigade posted at the ruined tower southwest of Brill. Zygand declares that the death will please the Dark Lady, and vows to herd the Crusade like cattle to its end.
sources: quest 427 description (documents Arren provided give their locations)
quest 370 description, completion and reward texts

parts.body: Next falls Captain Vachon, slain with his friars at the ruined tower near the Balnir Farmstead, from which they raided southeastern Tirisfal. His death will slow the Crusade's advance in the glades a good deal, Zygand judges, but other threats loom, and the papers point to one more commander in the north.

Last of all the ruthless Captain Melrache dies with his two bodyguards at the tower in the far north past Faol's Rest. With the Crusade's captains in Tirisfal cut down, Zygand praises the ruthless fighters who conquer in the Forsaken's name, for they bring his people one step closer to defeating Arthas once and for all.

title: The Fall of House Agamand
body: The Agamands were the wealthiest family in Tirisfal, and their pride became their ruin. When the Scourge came, Gregor Agamand would not abandon his mills. He fortified his home and talked his workers into staying to fight, and all of them were doomed to undeath. Now the dead Agamands serve the Scourge, who mean to make the mills a base for attacks across Tirisfal, and the Deathguard of Brill send fighters to clear the fields. Coleman Farthing, once a worker at the mills, wants the remains of Gregor, Nissa, Thurman and Devlin Agamand brought to him. Somewhere among the dead at the mills lies a letter from Thurman, the elder son, to Yvette Farthing, which never reached her.
notes: Check: part 2 (DONE 354 or DONE 362) trimmed to what both turn-ins reveal (Coleman's revenge, the Agamands destroyed), dropping Devlin's bones (362 only); Sevren's order moved to a new part 3 on DONE 355 or ACCEPT 408 (355 follows 354 and is not offered on 362; 408's description gives the crypt and Dargol); the crypt assault is now part 4. Part 1's last line paraphrases the letter more closely. Converted: Devlin's betrayal moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 361, which gives the readable letter); Coleman's revenge and Sevren's order against the crypt moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 354 or 362); the crypt assault's outcome moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 408). Yvette's reaction is told in 8522. Earlier: verified

parts.body: Thurman's letter tells what the family never lived to tell. His brother Devlin despaired and made a pact with the Scourge. One night he murdered two watchmen and let the undead through a breach, leading them to where many slept, and a third of the defenders died in the ambush. Thurman wrote knowing the family line would end. He did not regret staying with his family, and his last thoughts were for Yvette.
sources: page_text 214, 252-256 (Thurman's Letter, item 2837, given on accepting 361)

parts.body: Coleman takes the Agamand remains with grim satisfaction. Each one brought to him is another of the proud family destroyed, the family whose pride doomed him to undeath, and in their destruction the old mill worker finds what comfort revenge can give.

But the mills threaten all the Forsaken, not Coleman alone. Word of the work reaches Magistrate Sevren, who marks the Agamand Family Crypt for destruction, for there the Scourge commander Captain Dargol has raised the Agamand ancestors by necromancy to use against the Forsaken.

At the family crypt the raised ancestors are cut down and Captain Dargol's skull is carried to Sevren. The blow will not go unnoticed, the magistrate says, by the Forsaken or by their enemies, and he urges the struggle on until the Lich King himself is driven from Azeroth.

title: A New Plague
body: Lady Sylvanas has challenged the Royal Apothecary Society to create a new plague, deadlier than any ailment on Azeroth, to bring Arthas's Scourge to ruin. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan pursues the task by trial and error. He tests the blood of darkhounds, then the scales of murlocs, for plaguing a whole world proves harder than poisoning one victim, and then, after finding an old text about an ancient plague preserved in spider venom, the poison of the vicious night web spiders of eastern Tirisfal. Pumpkins stolen from the Solliden Farmstead serve him too. One, laced with his latest formula, is carried to a starving Scarlet zealot held in the cellar of the Gallows' End Tavern.
notes: Check: ok. Converted: the zealot's death moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 407); the finished brew and the mountaineer's drink moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 369, QUEST_ACCEPT 492); the mountaineer's death and the findings sent to Silverpine moved to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 492). 445 is cited only, not a trigger. Earlier: verified

parts.body: The half starved zealot cannot resist the gift. Within moments he stammers that he does not feel right, that his mind and flesh are rotting, and he is twisted into the shape of a ghoul before he falls dead. A simple pumpkin, as Johaan promised, has become an agent of the Dark Lady.
sources: quest 407 description, completion and reward texts

parts.body: With the venom added and the brew boiled down, Johaan's deadly new agent is ready to try. He mixes a special drink for a dwarven mountaineer the Deathguard have just captured, one that holds, he says, a subtle hint of what the Dark Lady has planned for the rest of Azeroth.

The mountaineer, still boasting that the Steam Tank Brigade will come to rescue him, takes the drink gladly and raises it in a defiant toast. Moments later he falls dead. Johaan sends his findings on to his colleagues of the Society at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, so that their joined work might one day give the Dark Lady her New Plague.

title: The Prodigal Lich
body: Bethor Iceshard, a high-ranking mage of the Undercity, asks Magistrate Sevren for an agent of proven worth against the Scourge. Sevren knows only that the task means recruiting a wayward lich, and that it will be dangerous. The lich dwells on an island in Brightwater Lake. He is free-willed, yet believes every other undead a Scourge slave and sets his minions on all who approach. Because he is Forsaken the Dark Lady will want him, and if he is skilled in necromancy his knowledge would be of great use. To learn who he is and what he can do, Bethor needs the lich's spellbook, so the agent must steal into his camp and take it.
notes: Check: ok. Converted: the lich's identity and the Kirin Tor past moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 357); the returned book and Gunther's demand to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 366); Lillith's death and the Nether Gem to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 409); Bethor's reply to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 411). Bethor 1498 and quests 405, 357, 366, 411 are not used by the Undercity file. Earlier: verified

parts.body: Bethor opens the book and is astonished: it belongs to Gunther Arcanus, his friend and comrade before the Plague. Long ago the two of them studied among the Kirin Tor of Dalaran with Thule Ravenclaw, now a necromancer of the Scourge. Bethor enchants the book so that it will show Gunther he too is free of the Lich King, and has it carried back to the island.

Gunther recognizes Bethor's enchantment and wonders whether his old friend truly escaped. Before he believes anything he wants proof that the thief is no Scourge slave, so the agent must light a Candle of Beckoning on a bloody altar off the island's southern shore and destroy Lillith Nefara when she wakes.

Lillith Nefara falls. Gunther had believed he was the only undead with free will, and now he knows others have broken the Lich King's domination. He gives the agent a Nether Gem to carry to Bethor, so that the two old friends can speak again.

The Nether Gem reaches Bethor in the Undercity, and with it word that Gunther will join the Forsaken. It is a great deed, Bethor declares. The Forsaken have won a powerful ally in the lich of Brightwater Lake, and the Dark Lady will be told of it.

title: The Graverobbers
body: When the Plague first came to Tirisfal, the dead were so many that mass graves were dug southwest of Garren's Haunt. Those bodies have so far been spared undeath, but the Scourge now send the Rot Hide gnolls to dig them up and carry them off to swell the Lich King's armies. Magistrate Sevren will not allow it. The Rot Hides are hunted at the graves and at Garren's Haunt, and the embalming ichor that animates them is gathered for study. Brill has also sentenced Maggot Eye, the foulest of the corpse thieves, to death. Nearby, a junior apothecary in the Brill graveyard waits impatiently on an abomination named Gordo, sent out to pick weeds by the graves.
sources: quest 446 description (Thule leads the Rot Hides)
notes: Check: confirmed silverpine.json tells Thule commanding the Rot Hides (13000, 13010, 13021, 13027), so the drop loses nothing. Converted: dropped the line that the Rot Hides answer to Thule Ravenclaw: it rests on quest 446, the Silverpine chain's reveal, which silverpine.json tells (13019, 13021). The ichor's fate moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 358), Maggot Eye's death to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 398), Gordo's wrong weeds to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 5481). Earlier: Thule link reworded: quests 444/446 belong to the Silverpine chain (443 from Renferrel), not to the Tirisfal ichor from 358, so the 'warlock and necromantic magic' finding was removed and Thule is given only as the Rot Hides' master (quest 446).

parts.body: The Scourge are mistaken, Sevren declares, if they think those corpses can be turned against the Forsaken. The ichor drained from the Rot Hide slaves goes to the apothecaries of the Society, for it may hold secrets the Forsaken can use against the Scourge.

Maggot Eye is dead, and his paw is laid before Executor Zygand. The town of Brill counts his crimes avenged, and Zygand hopes the deed sends a clear message to all who would bring harm to the Forsaken.

Gordo comes back with gloom weed, which is no use at all. Junior Apothecary Holland fumes that the mindless mass of flesh is out picking the wrong plants and drawing who knows how many helpers into the same mistake, and he sends a more capable one after what he truly needs: doom weed from the mass graves.
